availability.comment: Penix completed 20 of 31 passes for 162 yards and a touchdown with an interception in Sunday's 34-17 loss to Cincinnati. He added 50 rushing yards on three carries. It looked like it would be a big day for the Falcons offense when Penix led his team to points on its first two drives. including a one-yard TD to Charlie Woerner, but Atlanta managed just seven more points over the final three quarters. The touchdown pass was Penix's 10th of the season, setting a new career high, but he's also been picked off five times in the last two games after throwing only one INT in his first five contests of 2026. He'll face a tough test in Week 10 against Kansas City.

Robinson carried the ball 19 times for 100 yards and a touchdown and caught six of seven targets for 47 yards in Sunday's 34-17 loss to the Bengals. Backup Khalil Herbert handled just three touches, as Robinson dominated the workload in the Atlanta backfield with his usual No. 2, Brian Robinson (hamstring), on the shelf. It was the first time since Week 4 that Bijan had reached the century mark in rushing yards, and also the first time since that game against the Saints he got into the end zone. Robinson will look to build upon this effort in Week 10 against Kansas City.

London caught all five of his targets for 68 yards in Sunday's 34-17 loss to the Bengals. Cincinnati's secondary did a good job of limiting London's looks from Michael Penix, but the fifth-year wideout still led Atlanta in receiving yards, although Bijan Robinson caught one more pass and Charlie Woerner hauled in the QB's only touchdown. London has gotten only 11 targets over the last two games, turning them into a disappointing 6-76-0 line, and he could have a hard time breaking out in Week 10 against a stingy Kansas City secondary.

Dotson caught two passes for 16 yards on two targets in Sunday's 34-17 loss to the Bengals. Despite playing 84 percent of the offensive snaps, Dotson's two targets were a distant sixth on the team against Cincinnati. He has 16 catches for 33 yards and two touchdowns on 33 targets through nine games this season and isn't a particularly exciting fantasy option fighting for scraps behind Drake London, Bijan Robinson and Kyle Pitts in Atlanta.

Zaccheaus caught one of three targets for five yards during the Falcons' 34-17 loss to the Bengals on Sunday in Madrid. He also returned one kickoff for 28 yards and returned two punts for minus-three yards. Zaccheaus briefly left Sunday's game and was evaluated for a possible concussion, but the veteran wide receiver was quickly cleared to return. He has only six catches (on 16 targets) for 26 yards through eight regular-season games, and he's caught one pass or zero in seven of those contests. Zaccheaus isn't a key piece in the Falcons' offense, and that's unlikely to change heading into Week 10 against the Chiefs on Nov. 15.

Pitts caught three of five targets for 23 yards in Sunday's 34-17 loss to the Bengals. It was another quiet performance from Pitts, who hasn't reached 25 receiving yards in any of the last three games, and he had to watch backup tight end Charlie Woerner catch Michael Penix's only TD pass of the afternoon in the first quarter. Pitts will take a 25-220-4 line on 37 targets through nine contests into a Week 10 clash with Kansas City.

Mahomes (right elbow/knee) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice. As were Rashee Rice (knee) as well as Xavier Worthy (hamstring), and with Chiefs having added Josh Downs (who is not on the injury report) via a trade with the Colts, the team heads into Sunday's game against the Falcons with its franchise QB and top three WRs presumably available for Week 10 action. Mahomes clearly endured some elbow discomfort during the Chiefs' Week 9 win over the Jets, but the issue is something he'll continue to play through.

Walker rushed 18 times for 102 yards and a touchdown and brought in all four targets for 41 yards and two more scores in the Chiefs' 35-12 win over the Jets on Sunday. Walker put together another one of his signature high-efficiency performances on the ground, averaging 5.7 yards per carry in the process. He contributed a seven-yard touchdown reception on the first play of the second quarter, and he struck again as a receiver via a 25-yard scoring grab with just over five minutes remaining in the first half. Walker capped off the highly fantasy-friendly day with his seventh rushing touchdown of the season, a two-yard run in the waning moments of the third quarter. Walker is up to 872 rushing yards, 172 receiving yards and 11 total touchdowns heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Falcons next Sunday.

Rice secured five of seven targets for 49 yards in the Chiefs' 35-12 win over the Jets on Sunday. Rice led the Chiefs in targets while finishing as the runner-up in both receptions and receiving yards. The veteran receiver has been busy the last two games while turning 15 targets into a 12-102-1 line, but he has just one catch of 20-plus yards in that span. Rice is averaging a relatively modest 11.7 yards per catch heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Falcons.

Worthy (hamstring) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice for Kansas City. Worthy was considered day-to-day after exiting Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets in the fourth quarter. A quick return to full practice participation suggests Worthy will be fine for the upcoming matchup with Atlanta on Sunday, but his target share may decline in the second half of the season after Kansas City traded for WR Josh Downs.

Kelce brought in four of six targets for 72 yards in the Chiefs' 35-12 win over the Jets on Sunday. He also rushed once for one yard. Kelce led the Chiefs in receiving yards and finished second in targets on the afternoon, and his tally in the former category also served as the legendary tight end's second highest of the season. Kelce got there with a big boost from a game-high 38-yard catch, and he'll take a formidable 33-482-2 line into a Week 10 road matchup against the Falcons next Sunday.

Jones will remain with the Colts through Tuesday's trade deadline after the team informed him Saturday that he won't be moved, Tom Pelissero of The Ringer reports. The update settles recent trade speculation around Jones and indicates Indianapolis plans to keep him on the roster into the offseason. It's a wonder why any team was even interested in trading for Jones in the first place, as he's consistently been one of the least productive quarterbacks in the league this season. He also failed to put anything meaningful on tape Sunday in the Colts' loss to the Cowboys, completing 20 of 34 passes for 180 yards, one touchdown and one interception against one of the league's worst on-paper defenses. The touchdown was a 55-yard hookup with Ashton Dulin, where Dulin did all of the work after the catch. Jones' interception late in the fourth quarter sealed another loss for Indianapolis.

The Colts informed Taylor that he won't be traded before Tuesday's deadline, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports. In order to move Taylor, Indianapolis was reportedly seeking a blockbuster trade package on par with what Carolina received in exchange for Christian McCaffrey back in 2022, but Pelissero relays that inquiring teams weren't willing to meet that price tag. As a result, Taylor -- who is under contract through 2028 -- will stick around in Indianapolis through the remainder of the campaign, though it's possible that the Colts entertain trade offers for the 27-year-old running back again during the offseason.

Treadwell logged 52 of the Colts' 64 snaps and was held without a reception on one target in Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys. Since drawing a season-high eight targets in a Week 5 loss to the Steelers, Treadwell has barely surpassed that total over the past four games combined. Despite handling snap shares north of 70 percent in each of those contests, Treadwell has mustered a 5-58-0 receiving line on 10 targets during that stretch. The Colts will have more target volume up for grabs after trading Keenan Allen to the 49ers and Josh Downs to Kansas City on Tuesday, and though Treadwell could be one of the beneficiaries, he still looks to be a low-upside fantasy option.

Warren may see more targets after the Colts traded wideouts Josh Downs and Keenan Allen on Tuesday, Chris Bumbaca of ColtsWire reports. The trade deadline went as well as possible for Warren's fantasy value, considering the Colts moved their top wide receivers but avoided an all-out purge. The only problem is that Warren is already averaging 7.6 targets per game (fourth among TEs) and producing just 39.3 receiving yards per game and 7.2 yards per catch. Efficiency has been the issue, not volume, and the Colts will likely lean on their running game after declining to trade RB Jonathan Taylor. Improved play from Warren and QB Daniel Jones would probably matter more than another increase in target share.

Gordon rushed 16 times for 55 yards and brought in his only target for nine yards in the Dolphins' 19-9 loss to the Lions on Sunday. Gordon worked in the lead role as expected but found running room at a premium against a game Lions defense. Gordon has at least Sunday's carry total in four straight games, but he's now seen his rushing yardage total decline in consecutive games. Jaylen Wright's inactive status due to a quadriceps injury helped Gordon's touch floor overall, and the latter should remain the top option in Miami's ground attack in a favorable Week 10 road matchup against the Colts next Sunday.

Douglas secured six of eight targets for 70 yards in the Dolphins' 19-9 loss to the Lions on Sunday. Douglas led the Dolphins in receptions, receiving yards and targets, as the rookie third-round pick continued to profile as one of Malik Willis' most reliable targets. Douglas' catch and target totals were also new career highs, while his yardage tally tied for the second highest of his nascent NFL tenure. Douglas should continue to play a key role in Miami's air attack over the second half of the season as the Dolphins look to continue cultivating their young talent.

Bell (knee) is listed as a limited participant on Wednesday's injury report, C. Isaiah Smalls II of the Miami Herald reports. This is likely just maintenance for Bell's surgically repaired knee. His role as the No. 3 wide receiver in Miami hasn't yielded much, with Bell drawing targets on just 16.7 percent of routes and catching only 44.4 percent of his targets. Things can't get much worse, at least from a statistical standpoint, with QB Kyle McCord replacing Malik Willis (abdomen) for at least the next four weeks.

Washington caught two of three targets for 21 yards during Sunday's 19-9 loss to the Lions. Washington was held in check by Detroit's suspect secondary, failing to reel in at least three passes for the first time this season. In addition, his 21 receiving yards were also a season low. The wide receiver has yet to exceed 70 receiving yards in a game this year, and he has reached the end zone only once. Washington will have an opportunity to get back on track against the sputtering Colts in Week 10.

Dulcich caught two of four targets for 14 yards in Sunday's 19-9 loss to the Lions. Entering play Sunday, Dulcich produced 13 grabs for 166 yards over his previous three games, but he took a big step back against Detroit on a day Malik Willis didn't have any answers, as he passed for just 128 yards. Dulcich doesn't catch touchdowns and plays in a low-volume, low-scoring offense, making him more of a TE2 headed into Week 10 against the Colts.

Love completed 23 of 29 passes for 372 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed once for a 13-yard score in the Packers' 45-27 win over the Patriots on Sunday. He also ran in a two-point conversion. Love continued to attack downfield with great efficacy in the significant road upset for the Packers. Love averaged 12.8 yards per attempt while amassing his second-highest passing yardage total of the season, a figure bested only by the 387-yard tally he managed in Week 1. Love generated his second straight three-touchdown day through the air as well, connecting with Matthew Golden (five yards), Savion Williams (10 yards) and Christian Watson (39 yards) for his trio of scoring strikes and kicking off the scoring on the day with a 13-yard rush just 1:41 into the contest. Love is up to 2,618 passing yards with a 19:6 TD:INT and a pair of rushing scores heading into a Week 10 home divisional clash against the Vikings next Sunday.

Johnson could serve as the Packers' lead option on the ground in Sunday's game against the Vikings with Josh Jacobs (finger) expected to miss multiple weeks and with the status of MarShawn Lloyd (knee) uncertain, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports. After being a healthy inactive for the Packers' previous two games, Johnson suited up for Sunday's tilt with the Patriots while Lloyd was inactive. With Jacobs leaving the contest late in the first quarter after fracturing his right ring finger, Johnson was thrust into action and delivered the Packers' best rushing performance of the season, finishing with 14 carries for 68 yards and a touchdown in the 45-27 win. Head coach Matt LaFleur relayed Monday that Jacobs will need surgery and could land on injured reserve, and while Lloyd could have a chance at returning to action Week 10, the Packers likely came away encouraged enough by Johnson's showing in Foxborough to give him another turn as their lead option on the ground. Johnson isn't likely to earn much passing-down work, however, as Lloyd, Pierre Strong and Chris Brooks (ankle) -- who could return from IR this week -- are all more capable options in that phase.

Strong rushed eight times for 22 yards in Sunday's 45-27 win over the Patriots. He added two catches for 11 yards on two targets. With Josh Jacobs (finger) knocked out of the game in the first quarter and set to miss several weeks, Strong figures to see his role expand in Green Bay's backfield, though MarShawn Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson and even Chris Brooks (ankle) are likely to also see snaps in the coming weeks. Strong is not a recommended fantasy target in 12-team leagues.

Watson secured seven of eight targets for 171 yards and a touchdown in the Packers' 45-27 win over the Patriots on Sunday. Watson repeatedly got the best of Christian Gonzalez and the rest of a talented Patriots secondary, recording team- and career-high receiving yardage totals along the way. Watson burned New England for four catches of 20-plus yards, including a game-long 49-yard grab, as well as a 39-yard touchdown reception in the latter portion of the third quarter. Watson's career-best line is up to a tally of 49-879-7 on 74 targets heading into a Week 10 home matchup against the Vikings next Sunday.

Golden brought in all 10 targets for 164 yards and a touchdown in the Packers' 45-27 win over the Patriots on Sunday. Golden led the Packers in receptions and targets while finishing second in receiving yards, and the latter total was also a new career high. The second-year wideout also laid claim to the game's longest catch (49 yards), and he reeled in the first of Jordan Love's three TD passes on the day with a five-yard grab at just under the eight-minute mark of the first quarter. Golden now has four 100-yard efforts in what is already a breakout campaign that's seen him amass a 53-783-5 line on 92 targets heading into a Week 10 home showdown against the Vikings next Sunday.

Williams (groin) was limited in Wednesday's jog-through practice. It's a new injury for Williams, who previously missed a chunk of the season with an ankle injury. He's been running as the Packers' clear third receiver behind Matthew Golden and Christian Watson over the last few weeks. If Williams is unable to play against Minnesota on Sunday, Bo Melton and J. Michael Sturdivant could see an uptick in snaps, though Skyy Moore (ankle) had his 21-day practice window opened and could also be an option.

Kraft brought in one of three targets for one yard and rushed twice for eight yards in the Packers' 45-27 win over the Patriots on Sunday. The athletic tight end didn't get in on any of the fun on a day when Jordan Love threw for 372 yards and three touchdowns. Kraft's stat line set (receptions, receiving yards) or tied (targets) season lows, while his work on the ground included a pair of season-high figures. Nevertheless, it was an utterly forgettable showing for Kraft, who'll look to atone in a Week 10 home divisional clash against the Vikings next Sunday.

Wentz (ankle) is listed as limited on Wednesday's estimated practice report, Ben Goessling of The Minnesota Star Tribune reports. Wentz injured his ankle Monday night during his disastrous start against the Bills. The Vikings have since traded for Kirk Cousins, who likely will take over as the starter for Sunday's game at Green Bay. Coach Kevin O'Connell wouldn't commit to starting Cousins and suggested Kyler Murray (hamstring) is unlikely to play, but Cousins' familiarity with the scheme and terminology means he shouldn't need long to prepare.

Jones rushed five times for 16 yards and brought in his only target for five yards in the Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Bills on Monday night. Jones and backfield mate Jordan Mason combined for just 11 carries on an abysmal night for the Vikings offense, and the latter was much more efficient than Jones by averaging 5.8 yards per carry on his six totes. Jones now has seen his rushing yardage totals drop in three straight games, and Mason's return from injured reserve has played a role in the former seeing just 18 total carries in the last three contests. Jones retains a very modest outlook for a Week 10 road matchup against his old Packers teammates Sunday.

Mason rushed six times for 35 yards and brought in two of three targets for seven yards in the Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Bills on Monday night. Mason was markedly more efficient than backfield mate Aaron Jones with his opportunities, averaging 5.8 yards per carry compared to the latter's 3.2. Both backs' touches were limited due to game script, however, but Mason's YPC was an encouraging figure. The veteran back next takes aim at the Packers defense in a Week 10 road matchup on Sunday.
questionable questionable

Addison secured two of three targets for 28 yards in the Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Bills on Monday night. Addison finished third in receptions and receiving yards on the night for a low-volume Vikings passing game, and his final catch, which went for 16 yards, came on Minnesota's last drive from the arm of Max Brosmer. Carson Wentz's game-long ineffectiveness depressed the production of the air attack as a whole, but Addison would be in better position to boost his numbers if Kyler Murray (hamstring) is able to return for Sunday's Week 10 road matchup against the Packers.

Jefferson stands to benefit from Tuesday's acquisition of Kirk Cousins, who is expected to take over as the Vikings' starting quarterback beginning with Sunday's game against the Packers, Michael F. Florio of ESPN.com reports. Jefferson averaged a career-low 56.1 receiving yards per game through the first eight contests while the Vikings had the likes of Kyler Murray (hamstring), Carson Wentz and Max Brosmer under center, but the star receiver looks to be one of the biggest winners in the aftermath of the deadline. He'll be reunited with Cousins, who was at the helm for Jefferson's first four years in the league, when the wideout averaged 98.0 yards per contest and had a 17-game pace of 1,671 yards and 8.5 touchdowns. Though Cousins is three years older than when he last donned a Vikings uniform, he enjoyed a resurgent start to the season in Las Vegas, ranking second in the NFL in passing touchdowns (20) and fifth in passing yards (2,340) despite playing behind a weak offensive line and working with an underwhelming receiver group. Cousins' hot start and history with Jefferson should give Jefferson's fantasy managers added confidence in his rest-of-season outlook.

Hockenson (wrist/chest) is listed as a non-participant on Wednesday's estimated practice report. There was no clear sign of trouble Monday night when Hockenson played 83 percent of snaps in a loss to the Bills. A return to practice Thursday would put him on track to face the Packers this Sunday in what could be the first start of Kirk Cousins' second stint with the Vikings. Coach Kevin O'Connell declined to name a Week 10 starter Wednesday, but Cousins' familiarity with the offense seemingly gives him the edge over Carson Wentz (ankle) after Wentz's Monday night meltdown.
questionable questionable

Allgeier compiled 17 carries for 46 yards and caught two of three targets for no yards during Sunday's 17-3 defeat at Seattle. Allegeier has reeled off 10-plus touches in four straight contests, a span in which he's turned 65 touches into 334 yards from scrimmage and two total TDs. He's been the beneficiary of repeated ankle injuries to rookie first-round pick Jeremiyah Love, who must remain on IR for at least three more outings after Sunday's matchup, and the other current top RB on the active roster (Bam Knight) is in the concussion protocol, which will require clearance from an independent neurologist for his next game action. As a result, Allgeier is set up to retain a significant workload until Knight gets the all clear to return.

Duvernay registered two catches for eight yards on two targets, returned three kickoffs for 64 yards and brought back two punts for 21 yards in Sunday's 17-3 loss to the Seahawks. A two-time Pro Bowl return man, Duvernay played exclusively on special teams over the Cardinals' first seven games of the season, but he's seen his role on offense expand out of necessity following the trade of Marvin Harrison to the Texans along with the season-ending injuries to Kendrick Bourne (tibia) and Jalen Brooks (wrist). For the second straight week, Duvernay logged just under half of the offensive snaps, with his 45 percent share placing him behind only Michael Wilson (83 percent) and Simi Fehoko (49 percent) among the team's wideouts. Head coach Mike LaFleur announced Monday that Wilson was diagnosed with a neck fracture that will bring an end to his season, so Duvernay could be in line for an even more pronounced role heading into next Sunday's game against the Rams. However, with starting quarterback Gardner Minshew (elbow) also sustaining a likely season-ending injury in the loss to the Seahawks, Duvernay will be on the receiving end of passes from rookie third-round pick Carson Beck, who will make his NFL debut in Week 10.

Virgil caught one of four targets for 25 yards during Sunday's 17-3 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday. Gardner Minshew found Virgil for a 25-yard pass early in the first quarter, but the duo failed to connect for the rest of Sunday's contest. The Cardinals' offense took some big hits in Week 9, with Minshew sustaining a torn UCL and wide receiver Michael Wilson suffering a fracture in his neck, and those injuries will keep both players on the shelf for the rest of the 2026 season. Kendrick Bourne (lower leg) and Jalen Brooks (wrist) are both also on season-ending IR, which leaves Virgil, Simi Fehoko, Devin Duvernay and superstar tight end Trey McBride as the top targets for rookie third-round quarterback Carson Beck heading into Week 10 against the Rams.

Higgins caught both of his targets for 11 yards in Sunday's 17-3 loss to the Seahawks. With all of the injuries at wide receiver for Arizona, Higgins played a season-high 66 percent of the offensive snaps in Seattle. It still didn't translate to an elevated role in the pass game. Higgins has 18 grabs for 162 yards and a touchdown on 20 targets across nine games this season.

McBride recorded seven catches (on eight targets) for 54 yards during Sunday's 17-3 loss at Seattle. With QB Jacoby Brissett getting traded to Baltimore this past week, McBride was on the receiving end of passes from Gardner Minshew, and the result was the tight end's fourth-fewest receiving yards in a game this season and also the fourth time he didn't reach the end zone through nine contests. On a positive note, McBride extended his streak with at least seven receptions to 11 outings, which matches the second-longest streak in NFL history, trailing only the 14 Antonio Brown put together from 2014-2015. McBride may have a tough task on his hands next Sunday against the Rams' surging defense.

Stafford completed 26 of 43 passes for 228 yards and a touchdown with an interception in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders. He added one yard on his only carry. The veteran QB looked the way of Puka Nacua (knee) early and often, with no other Ram pass catcher managing more than 20 receiving yards, and the star wideout was on the other end of a seven-yard TD toss in the fourth quarter that proved to be the winning score. Stafford has thrown a single touchdown pass in back-to-back games after producing multiple TDs in five of six contests before that, and his options could get even thinner with Nacua headed for an MRI after getting hurt on L.A.'s final possession.

Corum carried the ball 11 times for 58 yards and a touchdown and failed to catch either of his two targets in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders. The Rams' backfield has become a full-fledged timeshare, with Corum getting double-digit carries for a third straight game and out-producing Kyren Williams on the ground in Washington. Corum has gotten into the end zone in all three of those contests, punching in a one-yard score in the third quarter Sunday, and over that stretch he's amassed 224 rushing yards and three TDs while averaging 5.7 yards a carry. With Puka Nacua (knee) headed for an MRI, the Rams could lean even more heavily on their ground attack in a Week 10 tilt against the Cardinals.

Williams carried the ball 15 times for 45 yards and caught three of four targets for 16 yards in Sunday's 20-13 win over Washington. Blake Corum was the more productive Ram on the ground, turning 11 carries into 58 yards and a touchdown, but the offense mainly flowed through Puka Nacua on the afternoon. Williams failed to find the end zone for only the third time in nine games this season, and the 45 rushing yards were his lowest total since Week 1, although he has yet to reach 100 in any contest. The Los Angeles backfield has become a clear timeshare however, limiting Williams' upside heading into a Week 10 trip to Arizona.

Mumpfield caught both of his targets for 20 yards during Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders. Despite the lack of production, Mumpfield's 20 receiving yards ended up being second-most on the Rams behind Puka Nacua (150). The bigger news from Sunday's game was Nacua sustaining a PCL/MCL sprain in his knee and turf toe, and the superstar wide receiver is expected to miss at least one month while on injured reserve, per Sarah Bishop of ESPN.com. With Davante Adams (hamstring) also on IR until at least Week 11, that leaves the Rams with Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell and rookie sixth-rounder CJ Daniels as the top wide receivers for Matthew Stafford. The Rams hit the road for Week 10 against the Cardinals, whose defense has given up 19 passing touchdowns, which is second-most in the NFL behind the Raiders (20).

Atwell recorded two catches on five targets for 16 yards during the Rams' 20-13 win over the Commanders on Sunday. Atwell ended up finishing second among Rams wide receivers in both targets and offensive snaps behind Puka Nacua. However, the Rams' offense will have to undergo a sizable overhaul in the absence of Nacua, who suffered a sprained PCL/MCL in his knee as well as turf toe during Sunday's win, with the superstar wide receiver expected to be sidelined for at least a month while on injured reserve, per Sarah Bishop of ESPN.com. Davante Adams (hamstring) is also on injured reserve, so that leaves Atwell and Konata Mumpfield as the top healthy wide receivers on the Rams' 53-man roster, and rookie sixth-rounder CJ Daniels is also in position for a larger role on offense. The Rams will face the Cardinals in Week 10, and Arizona's defense has given up 19 passing touchdowns on the year, which is second-most in the league behind Las Vegas' 20.

Parkinson (ribs) was limited in Wednesday's practice, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports. Parkinson has seemingly been banged up all season, and the ribs are just the latest issue for the tight end. With Puka Nacua (knee/toe), Davante Adams (hamstring) and Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) vacating more than 45 percent of the Rams' targets, Los Angeles figures to lean heavily on its tight ends to try and get by without its top two receivers and top pass-catching tight end. Parkinson and Tyler Higbee will likely have prominent every-down roles in the coming weeks.
questionable questionable

Higbee caught one of five targets for 13 yards during Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders. Higbee was held to just one catch for a second consecutive game, although his 13-yard grab set the Rams up on the Commanders' one yard line and led to a rushing touchdown by Blake Corum on the next play. Higbee has only four catches over his last three games, but he figures to play a larger role in the passing game for at least the next month while Puka Nacua (knee/toe) is on injured reserve. The Rams will hit the road for Week 10 against the Cardinals, whose defense has given up six touchdowns to opposing tight ends this season, which ranks 25th in the NFL.

Head coach Kevin O'Connell said Wednesday that he isn't ready to commit to Cousins as the Vikings' Week 10 starting quarterback, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports. Minnesota acquired Cousins via trade from Las Vegas on Tuesday, but even though he has experience working under O'Connell from his previous stint with the team in 2022 and 2023, the coach will wait to make a decision. It appears Kyler Murray (hamstring) is set to miss another game Sunday at Green Bay, meaning Cousins, Carson Wentz (ankle) and Max Brosmer are the options to get the call this weekend.

Jeanty rushed six times for 25 yards while catching five of seven targets for minus-5 yards in Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers. The Raiders largely abandoned the run after going down 14-0 early, but Jeanty was more effective with his six carries than Mike Washington, who rushed six times for minus-3 yards and finished without a target. Sunday's even distribution in carries was a positive development for Jeanty, who had just two rushing attempts to Washington's 25 in the Week 8 win over the Jets. Jeanty still has more receiving yards (371) than rushing yards (362) and is averaging just 3.2 yards per carry heading into a difficult Week 10 matchup against Seattle's elite front seven.

Washington turned six carries into minus-three yards in Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers. The rookie running back wasn't targeted in the passing game. One week after getting a trial run as the Raiders' clear lead back, a game in which he produced 83 yards on 25 carries, Washington was out-snapped 32 to 17 by Ashton Jeanty against San Francisco. He's averaging just 3.9 yards per carry on 71 totes this season and has just three receptions, though it's worth noting that Jeanty has been even less efficient as a ball carrier with only 3.1 YPC. Washington is a fantasy bench stash, but the Raiders' rushing attack seems broken as a whole.

Nailor caught two of four targets for nine yards during Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers. Nailor was a non-factor on offense in Week 9, failing to reach double-digit receiving yards for the fourth time this season. The wide receiver has had a hard time getting into a groove in his first season with Las Vegas, catching 14 of 28 targets for 122 yards and a touchdown over eight contests so far.

Tucker caught four of eight targets for 55 yards during Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers. Tucker finished tied for the team lead in targets with tight end Brock Bowers, garnering at least five targets for the fifth time in the team's last six contests. The wide receiver rebounded well after being blanked in Week 8 versus the Jets, securing four or more receptions for the seventh time this season. Tucker has now reeled in 33 of 56 targets for 529 yards and four touchdowns over the Raiders' first nine games during the 2026 campaign.

Bowers caught seven of eight targets for 111 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers. He also rushed once for two yards and lost a fumble. Bowers had a 21-yard touchdown reception in the third quarter and came one yard short of scoring again on a 33-yard catch on a fourth-quarter drive that ended with a Kirk Cousins interception in the end zone. The star TE has reached 70 receiving yards in all seven of his appearances this season and is up to six touchdowns. Bowers came five receiving yards shy of his season high and continues to roll, even as the 4-5 Raiders drop out of contention in the AFC. He'll likely face more resistance in Week 10 against the Seahawks, who just held Cardinals TE Trey McBride to 54 yards.

Mayer caught all three of his targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers. The tight end was inches and a couple breaks away from having a much bigger afternoon, as he lost a fumble just before crossing the goal line on what would have been a 25-yard touchdown. He then had another score called back on a penalty in the second half. Mayer has alternated big games with down ones this season, and he'll try to rebound next Sunday in a tough spot against the Seahawks' strong defense.

Lock (right elbow/oblique) was limited at Wednesday's practice, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports. Lock is tending to a lingering right elbow injury and a new oblique issue, which head coach Mike Macdonald said tests Monday that came back "good," and it'll be managed as Week 10 prep goes on, per Gregg Bell of Sports Radio 93.3 KJR Seattle. Lock's ability to begin the week with some practice reps generally is a good sign, but his status will continue to be watched to ensure he's good to start Sunday's contest at Las Vegas.

Wilson didn't log any snaps during Sunday's win over the Cardinals. Wilson averaged 18.2 carries for 66.7 yards over six games between Week 2 and Week 7, culminating with a 24-100-1 rushing line against Kansas City. However, that opportunity came while Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet were on IR. Both running backs returned ahead of the Week 8 matchup against Chicago, and Wilson hasn't played a single offensive snap in two games since. As long as Charbonnet and Price are both healthy, it appears Wilson is going to be relegated primarily to a special-teams role, if he plays at all.

Price posted nine carries for 24 yards and secured all four targets for 54 yards during Sunday's 17-3 victory versus the Cardinals. Price received one more touch than Week 8's 12 but more than doubled his yards from scrimmage from 37 to 78. Having said that, backfield mate Zach Charbonnet went from nine touches last Monday against the Bears to 17 in Week 9 while pacing the Seahawks in total yards with 86. Price and Charbonnet appear poised to split the RB reps moving forward, but the former may be the change-of-pace option while the latter handles early downs.

Charbonnet took 16 carries for 77 yards and tallied one catch (on two targets) for nine yards during Sunday's 17-3 win versus the Cardinals. The script in the Seahawks backfield flipped from Week 8 to this Sunday, as Charbonnet nearly doubled his touch count (nine vs. 17) while Jadarian Price maintained it (12 vs. 13). Charbonnet also was far more effective with his workload, going from 29 yards from scrimmage to 86. This marked only his second outing since tearing his left ACL back in January, so he figures to keep improving his efficiency while seemingly taking on a greater share of the RB reps over Price.

Kupp caught three of four targets for 32 yards during the Seahawks' 17-3 win over the Cardinals on Sunday. All three of Kupp's catches came on the same offensive drive midway through the third quarter, which ended with a 45-yard field goal by Jason Myers. The Seahawks had Drew Lock under center due to the absence of Sam Darnold (quadriceps/ribs), but Lock is now dealing with an oblique injury that could prevent him from playing in Week 10 against the Raiders on Nov. 15. Jalen Milroe would be the next man up at quarterback for Seattle, which would lower the floors for Kupp and the rest of the Seahawks' pass catchers. Kupp has a 22-238-2 receiving line on 34 targets through nine regular-season games.

Smith-Njigba reeled in seven of 10 targets for 51 yards during Sunday's 17-3 win against the Cardinals. Smith-Njigba was working with backup QB Drew Lock for the third time this season, as the latter was filling in for Sam Darnold (quadriceps/rib). The result was a season low in receiving yards, which was only the second time this season in which Smith-Njigba failed to reach the century mark. Despite the subpar outing for him, he surpassed 1,000 yards on the campaign for a third straight season, with eight games still to go. Darnold may also be sidelined next Sunday at Las Vegas, which again could impact Smith-Njigba's chances to produce as he has most weeks in 2026.

Horton caught two passes for 22 yards on three targets in Sunday's 17-3 win over the Cardinals. Horton has just seven catches for 67 yards across six games since Week 3. The Seahawks' No. 3 receiver is well off the fantasy radar, even with Rashid Shaheed (knee) injured.

Barner caught two of four targets for seven yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 17-3 win over the Cardinals. He added three carries for three yards and an additional touchdown. Barner was the Seahawks' closer, finishing off both touchdown drives with short scores against Arizona. His first was a one-yard rushing touchdown, and Barner then caught a seven-yard score from Drew Lock. Both touchdowns came in the second quarter. For the season, Barner has 23 grabs for 210 yards and one touchdown on 38 targets. He's also rushed for two scores. Barner is in the large group of touchdown-or-bust fantasy options at tight end.

Prescott completed 21 of 34 passes for 335 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions while rushing twice for one yard in the Cowboys' 27-23 win over the Colts on Sunday. He also lost a fumble. Prescott had a couple of bumps in the road against an inconsistent Colts defense, but the veteran signal-caller, who was also working without George Pickens (hamstring), still found his way to his third 300-yard effort of the season. Prescott unsurprisingly bestowed plenty of attention on CeeDee Lamb, who ultimately was responsible for 10 of his completions, 195 of his yards and one of his two TDs. Prescott also connected with Jake Ferguson for a 10-yard scoring strike early in the second quarter, and the one blemish on the star quarterback's day was a  fumble on a sack at his own 16-yard line that led to a Colts touchdown. Prescott has at least one touchdown pass in every game heading into a Week 10 home showdown against the 49ers next Sunday.

Williams rushed 20 times for 101 yards and a touchdown and brought in four of five targets for 23 yards in the Cowboys' 27-23 win over the Colts on Sunday. Williams turned in one of his more efficient performances against an inconsistent Colts defense, ultimately managing his second 100-yard effort of the season. Williams continued to serve as a prolific supplier of touchdowns as well, recording his ninth rushing score of the campaign on a one-yard run with 1:08 remaining to seal the victory for Dallas. Williams' week-to-week yardage production has fluctuated a fair amount, but his high-volume role and trusted red-zone presence keeps him a must-play despite a tough Week 10 home matchup against the 49ers next Sunday.

Lamb brought in 10 of 16 targets for 195 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys' 27-23 win over the Colts on Sunday. He also lost a fumble. Lamb easily led the Cowboys across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets in a game that Dallas was operating without George Pickens (hamstring). Lamb's yardage total was a new season high, and he rounded out his stellar day with his seventh touchdown catch of the campaign on a 44-yard grab just before halftime. Even his turnover had a bright side to it from a fantasy perspective, as Lamb gained 44 yards on an impressive downfield catch and picked up extra yardage after the Colts initially failed to touch him down before fumbling at the end of that sequence. Lamb has four straight double-digit target games and is just 96 yards away from his sixth consecutive 1,000-yard season heading into a Week 10 home showdown against the 49ers next Sunday.

Flournoy caught two of three targets for 53 yards during Sunday's 27-23 win over the Colts. Flournoy had a chance to operate in a more prominent role on offense with George Pickens (hamstring) inactive, but Flournoy ultimately finished with his fewest catches since Week 3, despite playing 77 of 79 offensive snaps. The wide receiver helped set up Dallas for the game-winning score late in the fourth quarter, reeling in a deep ball from quarterback Dak Prescott for a 46-yard gain. Flournoy now has reeled in 32 of 47 targets for 395 yards and two touchdowns over nine contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

Spann-Ford caught two of three targets for 20 yards during Sunday's 27-23 win versus the Colts. Spann-Ford opened Week 9 in his typical reserve role behind Jake Ferguson at tight end, but Ferguson suffered a knee injury in the third quarter. With Ferguson set to miss multiple weeks of action, Spann-Ford will have a chance to operate as the team's primary option at tight end beginning in Week 10 versus the 49ers. On the season thus far, Spann-Ford has reeled in 19 of 27 targets for 136 yards and four touchdowns over nine contests.

Purdy completed 17 of 25 passes for 232 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders. He added seven rushing attempts for 40 yards and a touchdown. Purdy gave the 49ers a 14-0 lead with a one-yard rushing touchdown in the first quarter, then added a 12-yard touchdown pass to Christian McCaffrey in the second quarter and a 37-yard touchdown pass to Jordan Watkins in the third. Unfazed by the numerous injuries to San Francisco's wide receivers, Purdy has a 17:5 TD:INT through the air to go with a pair of rushing scores heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Cowboys. Having led the 49ers to a 7-1 record, the fourth-place finisher in the 2023 MVP race is making a strong case for the award at the halfway point of the 2026 campaign.

McCaffrey rushed 18 times for 68 yards and a touchdown while catching two of three targets for 19 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders. McCaffrey got banged up in San Francisco's Week 7 loss to the Falcons, but a Week 8 bye allowed his hamstring to heal, and the star running back handled 20 touches Sunday while scoring twice to bring his season total to 10 touchdowns. He capped San Francisco's opening drive with a one-yard touchdown run and added a 12-yard touchdown catch in the second quarter. Rookie third-round pick Kaelon Black led the 49ers with 70 rushing yards on 11 carries, but McCaffrey remains the lead back heading into a Week 10 trip to Dallas, during which CMC will try to extend a seven-game touchdown streak.

Black rushed 11 times for 70 yards but wasn't targeted in Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders. Black led the 49ers in rushing yards, finishing with two more than Christian McCaffrey, but McCaffrey operated as the clear lead back and scored twice on 20 touches. McCaffrey won't be unseated as the starter while healthy, but Black has started to earn a larger role, with double-digit carries for at least 63 rushing yards in consecutive games. The rookie third-round pick is averaging a solid 4.5 yards per carry heading into a Week 10 road game against the Cowboys.

Kittle caught four of seven targets for 58 yards in Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders. Kittle had at least three more targets than any teammate Sunday but finished 28 receiving yards shy of Jordan Watkins' team-leading total, while Brock Purdy's two touchdown passes went to Christian McCaffrey and Watkins. Sunday's output marked Kittle's third-lowest yardage total of the season, but the star TE recorded at least four catches for a seventh consecutive game. He'll look to add to his season totals of 38 catches for 483 yards and five touchdowns in Week 10 against the Cowboys.

availability.comment: Burrow completed 24 of 29 passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons. He added seven yards and a TD on three carries. It was a nearly flawless performance from Burrow, as he hit Ja'Marr Chase for a 47-yard score in the first quarter and tossed a pair of shorter TDs to Tee Higgins later in the contest. The superstar QB also got into the end zone on a goal-line sneak in the second quarter. It's the fourth straight game in which Burrow has produced at least four touchdowns, an incredible stretch in which he's completed 77.0 percent of his passes for 1,215 yards with a 16:3 TD:INT plus two more scores on the ground. The Bengals, not coincidentally, are 4-0 in that span. Burrow will look to stay locked in for a big AFC North clash against the Steelers in Week 10.

Brown carried the ball nine times for 57 yards and caught all three of his targets for 18 yards in Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons. Samaje Perine actually saw more volume on the ground with 11 carries for 43 yards, but most of his workload came in the fourth quarter as the Bengals were grinding down the clock. Brown has yet to top 80 rushing yards in a game this season and he hasn't gotten into the end zone since Week 1, a disappointing first half of the year for a running back who amassed at least 1,300 scrimmage yards with double-digit scores each of the prior two campaigns. Brown will look for an opportunity to break out in Week 10 during a crucial AFC North battle against the Steelers.

Meyers caught two passes for 47 yards on three targets in Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons. With Andrei Iosivas (thumb) on injured reserve, Meyers has settled in as the Bengals' third receiver behind target hogs Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Meyers would need an injury to one of those two to become relevant again in fantasy.

Chase caught 10 of 12 targets for 155 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons. The superstar wideout hit the ground running in Madrid, capping Cincinnati's first drive with a 47-yard touchdown catch from Joe Burrow. It was Chase's fourth straight game getting into the end zone, a stretch in which he's delivered a stellar 32-435-4 line on 45 targets, and Sunday's 155 receiving yards were a season high. He'll look to keep rolling in Week 10 during a crucial AFC North battle against the Steelers.

Higgins caught five of six targets for 32 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 34-17 win over Atlanta. While he didn't see big volume, Higgins made his opportunities count, connecting with Joe Burrow on a four-yard TD in the second quarter and an eight-yard score in the third. Higgins has hit paydirt five times in the last three games, and on the season he's produced a 48-758-6 line on 67 targets through eight contests. He'll look to extend his scoring streak in Week 10 during a crucial AFC North clash with the Steelers.

Gesicki caught both of his targets for 11 yards during Sunday's 34-17 win versus Atlanta. Gesicki entered Week 9 having scored a touchdown in five straight games, and he saw his streak come to an end Sunday. The tight end was able to reel in multiple passes for the second straight week and fifth time this season, but his 11 receiving yards left much to be desired. Gesicki has now reeled in 19 of 26 targets for 252 yards and six touchdowns over eight regular-season games so far this year.

Rodgers completed 13 of 25 passes for 172 yards with no touchdowns and one interception in the Steelers' 27-6 win over the Browns on Sunday. Jaylen Warren spearheaded the Steelers' attack with 143 rushing yards and a touchdown, and backfield mate Rico Dowdle added 56 yards and a score of his own. When combined with a highly effective effort by Pittsburgh's defense, there wasn't much production required of Rodgers and the air attack after much busier games leading into Sunday. Rodgers finished with season-low figures in completions, pass attempts, completion percentage and passing yards while failing to throw a touchdown pass for the first time since Week 2, but he's highly likely to revert to his prior pass-heavy ways in a Week 10 road showdown against the Bengals on Sunday night, Nov. 15, following a Week 8 bye.

Warren rushed 17 times for 143 yards and a touchdown and brought in one of two targets for no gain in the Steelers' 27-6 win over the Browns on Sunday. He also fumbled once but recovered. Warren tied his single-game career high in rushing yards with Sunday's performance, which was partly fueled by a season-long 51-yard run. Warren now has back-to-back 100-yard efforts on the ground for the first time this season, and he snapped a brief two-game rushing TD drought Sunday with a one-yard run early in the third quarter that closed out the scoring for the afternoon. Warren is already up to 704 rushing yards on a career-best 5.9 yards per carry heading into a Week 9 road showdown against the Bengals on Sunday, Nov. 15, following a Week 8 bye.

Dowdle rushed 15 times for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers' 27-6 win over the Browns on Sunday. Dowdle finished just two carries behind Jaylen Warren on the afternoon, and although his backfield mate significantly outpaced him in yardage, the former made his fantasy mark when he opened the scoring on the day with a nine-yard touchdown run in the first quarter. Dowdle recorded new season highs in rush attempts and rushing yards as the Steelers had the luxury of leaning heavily on the ground attack, but Warren remains the backfield's clear No. 1 option heading into the Week 9 bye.

Metcalf brought in one of six targets for four yards in the Steelers' 27-6 win over the Browns on Sunday. Aaron Rodgers put up a season low in completions, pass attempts, passing yards and completion percentage Sunday, and Metcalf's production was part of the collateral damage. The veteran wideout did see a team high in targets, but the fact he did next to nothing with them led to season lows in catches and receiving yards. Metcalf has had a handful of splash plays over the first half of the season and has two games of more than 90 receiving yards, but he's averaging a career-low 11.5 yards per catch and has just a single touchdown reception heading into the Week 9 bye.

Bernard caught all five of his targets for 30 yards during Sunday's 27-6 win against Cleveland. Bernard led the team in catches, reeling in multiple passes for the fifth straight week and sixth time overall this year. The wide receiver has built a strong rapport with starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers, but it's unclear what Bernard's workload will look like after the Steelers have a chance to regroup and potentially acquire another pass catcher during the team's bye week in Week 9.

Washington caught three of five targets for 94 yards during Sunday's 27-6 win over the Browns. Washington led the team in receiving yards while finishing tied for second on the team in targets with wide receiver Germie Bernard. The tight end's biggest moment of the game came in the third quarter when he reeled in a short pass from Aaron Rodgers and took off for a 58-yard gain. Washington has corralled 19 of 28 targets for 254 yards and three touchdowns over eight contests to open the 2026 regular season.

Freiermuth caught both of his targets for 35 yards in Sunday's 27-6 win over the Browns. He added one rushing attempt for a one-yard touchdown. With time expiring in the second quarter, Freiermuth took a direct snap and punched in a one-yard rushing score to put the Steelers up 20-6 headed into halftime. The tight end entered the season with zero career carries but now has four through eight games, turning them into five yards and a touchdown. As a receiver, Freiermuth has been held to exactly two catches in each of the last three games and has yet to hit 50 yards in any game this season. He's a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet with the Steelers headed into their bye week.

Ahead of Week 10, Ravens head coach Jesse Minter noted "I expect (Brissett) to be our starter" next Monday against the Chargers, Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic reports. Brissett officially landed with the Ravens in a trade with the Cardinals this past Friday, and he's now on track to assume his new team's starting QB role for the foreseeable future. As a result, Joe Fagnano -- who had a spot start in Week 9 -- will revert to backup status. With regard to franchise signal-caller Lamar Jackson (thumb), who currently is on IR, he's indicated that he plans to return later this season. However, he's out for at least three more games, and 4-5 Baltimore's record as the season progresses figures to factor into Jackson's approach to a potential return to action.

The Ravens aren't expected to deal Henry before Tuesday's trade deadline, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. With Baltimore sitting at 4-5 and having lost its top two QBs in Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) for the foreseeable future and rest of the season, respectively, there has been speculation Henry may be available via trade, but the team has informed the running back that it doesn't intend to consider such a transaction. Instead, the Ravens have dealt for quarterback Jacoby Brissett from the Cardinals to help stabilize the offense, which may help Henry end his streak being held under 100 yards rushing at four contests. Overall, Henry has racked up 689 yards and eight touchdowns on 175 carries for a career-low 3.9 YPC in his nine appearances in 2026.

Hill rushed nine times for 85 yards and a touchdown and brought in all three targets for seven yards in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday night. Hill provided the sole offensive highlight of the night for the moribund, Joe Fagnano-led offense, making one cut after getting the handoff from the rookie quarterback halfway through the fourth quarter and bursting through the defense up the right side of the field for a 65-yard touchdown run. Hill's yardage total was both a team- and season-high figure for the veteran change-of-pace back, who should benefit from the pending trade acquisition of Jacoby Brissett from the Cardinals whenever the veteran signal-caller is able to take the reins of the offense.

Bateman caught one of two targets for six yards in Thursday night's 33-10 loss to the Jaguars. That's back-to-back one-catch games for Bateman with Joe Fagnano at quarterback for the Ravens. With Zay Flowers also healthy, Bateman has little fantasy appeal in season-long formats, though things could change when Jacoby Brissett takes over as Baltimore's starting quarterback in Week 10.

Flowers brought in three of six targets for six yards and rushed three times for 17 yards in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday night. Joe Fagnano drew the start with both Lamar Jackson (IR, thumb) and Tyler Huntley (IR, toe) out of action, and the rookie undrafted signal-caller averaged a microscopic 3.3 yards per attempt and threw two interceptions. Therefore, Flowers once again put forth a forgettable receiving line, although he at least got on the board with a trio of catches after being blanked on five targets in the Week 8 loss to the Bills. The Ravens tried to boost Flowers' touches with his trio of rush attempts, and he was reasonably effective with those. While fantasy managers have gotten next to nothing from the talented receiver over the last two games, Jacoby Brissett, who Baltimore is finalizing a trade for with the Cardinals, could be ready to suit up as soon as a Week 10 home matchup with the Chargers on Monday night, Nov. 16.

Andrews secured both targets for 19 yards in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday night. The veteran tight end actually led the Ravens in receiving yards with his modest total, as fill-in signal-caller Joe Fagnano averaged just 3.3 yards per attempt and totaled 60 passing yards overall. Andrews opened the season with back-to-back 49-yard tallies on 10 total catches, but he's been stuck at 28 receiving yards or fewer in his seven subsequent games. Andrews will hope to benefit from the pending trade acquisition of Jacoby Brissett, who should bring some stability and productivity to Baltimore's currently embattled quarterback situation.

Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said that Herbert "should be good to go" for Monday's game at Baltimore after imaging on the quarterback's injured left middle finger returned negative for a fracture, ESPN.com reports. Herbert may still have to manage some discomfort in the finger during Monday's contest, but since the injury to his non-throwing hand, he shouldn't be too affected while throwing or handing the ball off. That being said, Herbert has become increasingly difficult to justify including in fantasy lineups even when he's been in more optimal health entering games. Heading into the matchup with the Ravens, Herbert has completed a career-low 61.3 percent of his passes for 6.8 yards per attempt and just six touchdowns in eight games. He's tied with New England's Drake Maye for the league lead in interceptions thrown (11) and ranks second behind Cleveland's Deshaun Watson in sacks taken (31).

Vidal rushed seven times for 30 yards in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans. He added one catch for six yards on three targets. The Chargers continue to use a three-man backfield, an unfriendly fantasy situation and one to avoid when making lineup decisions each week. Vidal has been productive when he does get touches, rushing 36 times for 162 yards (4.5 YPC) and one touchdown across eight games. He's also caught 10 passes for 56 yards and an additional score.

Hampton rushed 13 times for 60 yards and wasn't targeted in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans. Hampton worked as the Chargers' primary rushing option ahead of Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal, who recorded seven carries apiece. The 0-8 Chargers unsurprisingly faced another negative game script, though, and Hampton wasn't involved in the passing game. The 2025 first-round pick continues to disappoint on a surprisingly awful offense that could get even worse should QB Justin Herbert (finger) miss any additional action after exiting in the fourth quarter. Hampton will try to snap a four-game touchdown drought in Week 10 against the Ravens.

Lambert-Smith registered one catch (on four targets) for 50 yards in Sunday's loss to Houston. Lambert-Smith wasn't exactly prolific in spite of logging a hearty 40 offensive snaps, but he made his one catch count, hauling in a 50-yard reception in the third quarter. However, the woeful Chargers turned the ball over on a fumble two plays later. Lambert-Smith has spent much of the season on IR and has had an inconsistent role when suiting up, but he was deployed pretty heavily Sunday because Ladd McConkey couldn't play due to back spasms. If McConkey is also sidelined next Monday in Baltimore, Lambert-Smith could again be a fairly big part of Los Angeles' air attack.

Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh noted Monday that McConkey is viewed as "day to day" with back spasms, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports. McConkey was not among the Chargers' Week 9 inactives, but he didn't play any snaps in Sunday's loss to the Texans after experiencing back spasms during pregame workouts. Harbaugh's assessment that the wideout is 'day-to-day' offers hope that McConkey will be in the clear ahead of next Monday's game against the Ravens, and a big step toward that outcome would be his full participation in practice no later than Saturday.

Johnston caught one of four targets for a 58-yard touchdown in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans. Johnston's long touchdown catch cut the deficit to 38-15 in the fourth quarter. That was the final pass Justin Herbert (finger) completed before exiting the game. If Herbert can't play against the Ravens in Week 10, Johnston would likely find himself catching passes from DJ Uiagalelei. Johnston's 58 receiving yards set a new season high, surpassing his one-catch, 57-yard effort in Week 6, and Sunday's TD was his first of the season.

Harris caught three of seven targets for six yards during Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans. Harris failed to take advantage of Ladd McConkey (back) failing to appear in Sunday's game, registering his fewest receiving yards in a game this season. Harris was able to garner a team-high seven targets, which bodes well for his chances of increased production in Week 10 against the Ravens if McConkey remains sidelined.

Gadsden caught two of three targets for 17 yards during the Chargers' 44-22 loss to the Texans on Sunday. Gadsden was on the field for 33 of 72 offensive snaps (45.8 percent), which was second-most among Chargers tight ends behind Charlie Kolar (47). Gadsden has caught two passes or fewer in six of eight regular-season games, and his 19-172-1 receiving line (on 29 targets) is well behind pace from his rookie campaign (49 catches on 69 targets for 664 yards and three scores across 15 regular-season contests). The Chargers' offense this season has struggled under quarterback Justin Herbert and coordinator Mike McDaniel, which doesn't bring much confidence ahead of their Week 10 road tilt against the Ravens on Monday Night Football.

availability.comment: Stroud completed 21 of 35 passes for 384 yards, five touchdowns and one interception and recorded two carries for 20 yards during Sunday's 44-22 win at the Chargers. Stroud matched a career high with his five TD strikes, which went to Xavier Hutchinson (17 yards), Tank Dell (63), Kayshon Boutte (12 and 63) and Nico Collins (13). Moreover, Stroud's 384 passing yards matched the second most in a game in his career. He's now thrown for multiple touchdowns in four of the last five games, a stretch in which he's accounted for a remarkable 1,457 yards through the air and a 13:2 TD:INT. Stroud will attempt to keep things rolling next Sunday, when the Texans visit the Browns.

Marks (knee) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports. In this past Sunday's 44-22 win over the Chargers, Marks played on 66 percent of the Texans' snaps on offense, while carrying 18 carries times for 70 yards and catching one of his four targets for four yards. He's been working as the team's clear-cut RB1 in the absence of David Montgomery (groin), who didn't practice Wednesday, with further context regarding the the backfield duo's Week 10 status on track to arrive no later than Thursday's practice report.

Boutte erupted for four catches (on five targets) for 125 yards and two touchdowns during Sunday's 44-22 road win against the Chargers. Boutte entered Week 9 action with a cumulative 15-194-0 line on 23 targets through seven appearances this season, so Sunday's performance was a true outburst. It didn't hurt that Boutte and his teammates were facing the only winless team in the NFL, but QB C.J. Stroud took full advantage of the opportunity, including Boutte (twice) among his five TD tosses. Ultimately, the Texans' receiving corps has a clear No. 1 in WR Nico Collins, who is the best bet among the group to produce most weeks.

Harrison (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday's practice, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports. It's a new injury for the Texans' newest wideout, who has produced just six catches for 60 yards and a touchdown on 11 targets through three games with Houston. Harrison ran just 14 routes on 40 dropbacks last Sunday against the Chargers, tying him with Kayshon Boutte for fourth among Texans wideouts. Xavier Hutchinson and Tank Dell appear to have emerged as the Nos. 2 and 3 receivers behind Nico Collins.

Collins corralled all four of his targets for 55 yards and one touchdown during Sunday's 44-22 victory at the Chargers. Collins was one of four Texans to reach the end zone via a pass from QB C.J. Stroud, who tossed five TDs in all. It marked Collins' first touchdown since Week 4, when he struck twice against the Cowboys, but overall his output from week to week this season has been a bit inconsistent, as he sits on a 28-384-4 line on 39 targets through his six appearances. He'll seek better results next Sunday in Cleveland.

Dell (hand) was limited in Wednesday's practice, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports. Dell operated as the Texans' third receiver for much of last Sunday's 44-22 win over the Chargers, running 22 routes on C.J. Stroud's 38 dropbacks. In just his second game since Week 16 of the 2024 campaign, Dell turned nine targets into five catches for 104 yards and a touchdown against Los Angeles. He's become a legitimate name to add in fantasy football ahead of Sunday's Week 10 date with the Browns.

Hutchinson caught three of five targets for 29 yards and a touchdown and  added a 28-yard kick return during Sunday's 44-22 win against the Chargers. Hutchinson finished tied with Kayshon Boutte for second on the team in targets behind fellow wideout Tank Dell (nine). Hutchinson was able to reach paydirt for the second straight contest, reeling in a 17-yard touchdown pass from C.J. Stroud for the team's first score of the day in the first quarter. There are many mouths to feed in Houston's passing attack, so Hutchinson will remain a volatile fantasy option ahead of the team's Week 10 matchup with the Browns.

Schultz caught two of four targets for 42 yards in Sunday's 44-22 win over the Chargers. Not counting his 12-140-0 receiving explosion in Week 2 when Nico Collins was out with a hamstring injury, Schultz has mustered 23 grabs for 244 yards and no touchdowns across his seven other appearances. He's failed to reach 50 receiving yards in any of those contests and is merely a TE2 in fantasy.

Jones will remain with the Colts through Tuesday's trade deadline after the team informed him Saturday that he won't be moved, Tom Pelissero of The Ringer reports. The update settles recent trade speculation around Jones and indicates Indianapolis plans to keep him on the roster into the offseason. It's a wonder why any team was even interested in trading for Jones in the first place, as he's consistently been one of the least productive quarterbacks in the league this season. He also failed to put anything meaningful on tape Sunday in the Colts' loss to the Cowboys, completing 20 of 34 passes for 180 yards, one touchdown and one interception against one of the league's worst on-paper defenses. The touchdown was a 55-yard hookup with Ashton Dulin, where Dulin did all of the work after the catch. Jones' interception late in the fourth quarter sealed another loss for Indianapolis.

The Colts informed Taylor that he won't be traded before Tuesday's deadline, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports. In order to move Taylor, Indianapolis was reportedly seeking a blockbuster trade package on par with what Carolina received in exchange for Christian McCaffrey back in 2022, but Pelissero relays that inquiring teams weren't willing to meet that price tag. As a result, Taylor -- who is under contract through 2028 -- will stick around in Indianapolis through the remainder of the campaign, though it's possible that the Colts entertain trade offers for the 27-year-old running back again during the offseason.

Treadwell logged 52 of the Colts' 64 snaps and was held without a reception on one target in Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys. Since drawing a season-high eight targets in a Week 5 loss to the Steelers, Treadwell has barely surpassed that total over the past four games combined. Despite handling snap shares north of 70 percent in each of those contests, Treadwell has mustered a 5-58-0 receiving line on 10 targets during that stretch. The Colts will have more target volume up for grabs after trading Keenan Allen to the 49ers and Josh Downs to Kansas City on Tuesday, and though Treadwell could be one of the beneficiaries, he still looks to be a low-upside fantasy option.

Warren may see more targets after the Colts traded wideouts Josh Downs and Keenan Allen on Tuesday, Chris Bumbaca of ColtsWire reports. The trade deadline went as well as possible for Warren's fantasy value, considering the Colts moved their top wide receivers but avoided an all-out purge. The only problem is that Warren is already averaging 7.6 targets per game (fourth among TEs) and producing just 39.3 receiving yards per game and 7.2 yards per catch. Efficiency has been the issue, not volume, and the Colts will likely lean on their running game after declining to trade RB Jonathan Taylor. Improved play from Warren and QB Daniel Jones would probably matter more than another increase in target share.
